claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option is never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes, independent of Pulumi's `protect` option.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection enforced by the cloud provider.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection enforced by the cloud provider.
The cloud provider enforces resource-level deletion-protection attributes (such as `deletionProtection`) independently of anything Pulumi knows about, including Pulumi's `protect` option.

A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (`protect` not set) and still refuse to delete because of the provider's own deletion protection, or conversely be protected in Pulumi while not having provider-side deletion protection.

The page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi `protect` and provider-side deletion protection apart and how to resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes that the cloud provider or cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi's `protect` resource option.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that provides deletion protection separate from Pulumi's `protect` option.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a cloud resource's own deletion-protection attributes are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' that explains how to tell Pulumi `protect` and resource-level deletion protection apart and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When `pulumi destroy` fails because of the `protect` resource option, the error message names the resource URN and mentions `protect`.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the `protect` resource option.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, e.g. `deletionProtection` on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` or `gcp.container.Cluster`; the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a `deletionProtection` argument.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a `deletionProtection` argument that is enforced by the provider.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection` is enforced by the AWS API, which rejects the delete call independent of Pulumi.
AWS EC2 `disableApiTermination` is enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection), which rejects the delete call independent of Pulumi.
An Azure Resource Manager management lock causes the delete call to be rejected by Azure independent of Pulumi.
When a cloud API rejects a delete due to a management lock, the error often carries a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked`.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the Pulumi program currently says.

For provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced deletion protection, setting the attribute to `false` in the program is not enough on its own; you must run `pulumi up` to apply the change to the live resource and state before `pulumi destroy` succeeds.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside of Pulumi (e.g. in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack state with reality and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the provider.
`gcp.bigquery.Dataset` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute; destroying a dataset that still contains tables fails unless it is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to `false`; a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute.
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to `false`.
`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist in the Pulumi Azure Native provider.
In Azure, a `CanNotDelete` management lock must be removed before the resource can be deleted, independent of anything in the Pulumi program.
Destroying an Azure Key Vault (`azure-native.keyvault.Vault`) only soft-deletes it.
Recreating an Azure Key Vault with the same name as a soft-deleted vault fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Azure Key Vault purge protection prevents purging a soft-deleted vault until its retention period elapses.
